- Version: 1.0.0

## 3. Parameters

None.

Reject illegal values at elaboration with `$error` inside a generate block.

## 4. Clocks, resets and clock-domain crossings

- Clocks: `aclk`.
- Resets: `aresetn`.
- Clock and reset behaviour, and any clock-domain crossing, as described in section 6.
- Every clock domain: name, frequency, source, the logic on it. Every reset: one per domain, synchronous active low inside the domain, entering the domain only through a reset synchroniser (asynchronous assertion, synchronous release); reset sequencing between domains has a single, documented source.
- Every clock, reset and signal boundary uses a clock-domain crossing technique, listed in the file header. Never sample another domain's signal directly; never pass a multi-bit value through independent single-bit synchronisers. Example techniques:

| Technique | Use for | Library module |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| Two- (or more) flop synchroniser (`async_reg`) | single slow level signal (enable, status, IRQ level) | `bit_sync` |
| Pulse synchroniser (toggle, sync, edge detect) | one-clock event / pulse | `pulse_sync`, `toggle_sync` |
| Reset synchroniser (async assert, sync release) | a reset entering a clock domain | `reset_sync`, `reset_ctrl` |
| Asynchronous FIFO with Gray-coded pointers | data stream at any rate ratio | `async_fifo`, `axis_async_bridge` |
| Request / acknowledge handshake (2- or 4-phase) | occasional multi-bit word, register access | `axi4_lite_cdc`, `clock_domain_bridge` |
| Multi-cycle path formulation (hold data, sync a qualifier) | multi-bit value that changes rarely | `cdc_sync_bit` + held register |
| Gray-code counter | counter value read in another domain | inside `async_fifo` |
| Glitch-free clock gate / mux | stopping or switching a clock | device BUFGCE / BUFGMUX, `clk_gen` enables |
| Related clocks from one PLL (fixed phase) | serializers, e.g. 10:1 TMDS, 7:1 LVDS | `clk_gen` outputs of one oscillator |

- Constrain every crossing (false path / max delay on the synchroniser's first flop) and document it.

## 5. Interfaces

- **s_axil_*** - AXI4-Lite slave, address [7:0], 32-bit data: interface `axil_if.slave` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axil_if.sv`).
- **s_axis_t*** - AXI4-Stream slave (input), tdata [7:0]: interface `axis_if.slave` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`).
- **m_axis_t*** - AXI4-Stream master (output), tdata [7:0], tlast: interface `axis_if.master` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`).

Bus ports follow the library's SystemVerilog interfaces, one definition file per type: AXI4-Stream `axis_if` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`, modports master / slave / monitor) and AXI4-Lite `axil_if` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axil_if.sv`, modports master / slave). Icarus Verilog cannot drive members of interface arrays and Yosys reads interfaces only through sv2v, so keep discrete ports (<prefix>_tdata, <prefix>_awaddr, ...) and put the interface and modport in a comment line directly above each port group: `// s_axis: axis_if.slave (ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv), DATA_W = 24`. Testbenches and Verilator flows may instantiate the interfaces directly.

| Port | Dir | Width | Group | Built when | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aclk` | input | 1 | - | - | - |
| `aresetn` | input | 1 | - | - | - |
| `sclk_o` | output | 1 | m_axis: axis_if.master (ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv), DATA_W = 8 | - | - |
| `cs_n_o` | output | 1 | m_axis: axis_if.master (ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv), DATA_W = 8 | - | - |
| `mosi_o` | output | 1 | m_axis: axis_if.master (ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv), DATA_W = 8 | - | - |
| `miso_i` | input | 1 | m_axis: axis_if.master (ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv), DATA_W = 8 | - | - |
| `irq_o` | output | 1 | m_axis: axis_if.master (ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv), DATA_W = 8 | - | - |

Back-pressure on every stream: honour tready, never drop data unless section 6 says so; valid must not depend combinationally on ready.

AXI4-Lite / register map: as listed in the behaviour text in section 6. Out-of-range accesses return SLVERR (or DECERR where stated).

## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference design's specification):

```text
SPI NOR flash controller (single-bit SPI mode 0, 3-byte
addressing, e.g. W25Qxx / S25FL / MX25). The
registers (cfg_* / sts_* ports; spi_flash_ctrl_top.sv is the block with
its AXI4-Lite register map, src/include/spi_flash_ctrl_regs.sv, ID "SPFL"
/ VERSION / DATE at 0x00-0x08) issue generic commands - write CMD (0x10)
with opcode[7:0], addr_en[8], dummy bytes[15:12], read_data[16],
write_data[17] after setting ADDR (0x14, 24 bit) and LEN (0x18, data
bytes 0..65535); the
controller then drives cs_n, sends opcode, address and dummy bytes and
moves LEN data bytes: bytes read from the flash leave on the AXI-Stream
master port (m_axis) and bytes to write are taken from the AXI-Stream
slave port (s_axis), each waiting for the stream handshake with sclk
stopped between bytes (so the flash never sees a gap it cannot handle,
and no byte is lost). Any flash command is expressible: 9F read ID, 03/0B
read, 06 write enable, 02 page program, 20/D8/C7 erase, 05 read status
(poll STATUS-of-flash yourself by issuing 05 with LEN=1). Registers -
0x10 CMD (write starts, reads back last), 0x14 ADDR, 0x18 LEN, 0x1C
CLKDIV (sclk half period in clocks, min 3, reset 4, so 12.5 MHz at 100
MHz), 0x20 STATUS (bit0 busy, bit1 done sticky, bit2 cmd_err sticky;
write 1 to clear bits 1 and 2), 0x24 IRQ_EN (bit0). A
CMD written while busy is ignored and sets cmd_err. irq_o = done &
IRQ_EN. Clock - aclk; miso is asynchronous and double-registered, which
is why the half period is at least 3 clocks. Reset - synchronous aresetn,
cs_n high, sclk low. Timing - cs_n is asserted one half period before the
first sclk edge, held one half period after the last, and kept high for
two half periods between commands. Latency - command starts 2 clocks
after the CMD write; data throughput is 8 bit times per byte plus stream
wait. The flash write-in-progress state is the flash's own business: poll
it with command 05. Errors - cmd_err (command while busy); a stalled
stream simply pauses the transfer.

spi_flash_ctrl with its AXI4-Lite register interface, the
block designs and testbenches instantiate: the register map
spi_flash_ctrl_regs (u_regs, src/include/spi_flash_ctrl_regs.sv, ID
"SPFL", VERSION and DATE at 0x00-0x08, the registers from 0x10) and the
logic spi_flash_ctrl (u_core, src/spi_flash_ctrl.sv), joined by their
register ports (cfg_* to the logic, sts_* back). Generated by
ip/scripts/regmap_gen.py from spi_flash_ctrl_regs.json and the ports of
spi_flash_ctrl: regenerate after changing either. Clock - aclk. Reset -
synchronous active low aresetn.
```

Describe and handle the edge cases, error recovery, latency and configuration-change rules stated above; where the text is silent, choose the safe option and document it in the file header.

## 6a. Industry reference check

Comparison of section 6 with published engineering references. Every difference is a `TODO(REF-...)` written as a prompt for updating the design.

```text
// Industry reference check - spi_flash_ctrl (2026-10-16)
// Sources:
//   [1] Winbond, "W25Q128JV 3V 128M-bit Serial Flash Memory" datasheet Rev. M (2024),
//   https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/7161/256_W25Q128JV.pdf - 8.1
//   instruction set (9Fh, 03h, 0Bh, 06h, 02h, 20h, D8h, C7h, 05h), SPI modes 0 and 3
//   [2] Motorola / Freescale, "SPI Block Guide V04.01", S12SPIV4/D (2004), https://web.pa.msu.e
//   du/people/edmunds/Disco_Kraken/SPI_Documents/motorola_freescale_nxp_spi_manual_2000.pdf -
//   CPOL / CPHA
// Published algorithm / equations:
//   W25Q128JV standard SPI: mode 0 or 3, command byte then 24-bit address (MSB first), 03h read
//   (no dummy, up to 50 MHz), 0Bh fast read (8 dummy clocks), 06h write enable before 02h page
//   program (<= 256 bytes, within one page) / 20h, D8h, C7h erase, 05h status register 1 (BUSY
//   = bit 0), 9Fh JEDEC ID; /CS must rise after a whole byte for program / erase to start.
// Comparison with this IP (section 6):
//   Matches: generic command sequencer (opcode, optional 3-byte address, dummy bytes, read or
//   write data) covers all listed commands, mode 0, MSB first, cs_n framing, BUSY polling left
//   to software. sclk stops between bytes while the stream waits (allowed: SPI flash is fully
//   static).
// Result: in line with the reference; no TODO.
```

### Register map (from `spi_flash_ctrl_regs.json`)

| Offset | Name | Access | Reset | Description | Fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x00 | ID | RO | "SPFL" | IP identifier, 4 ASCII characters (first in [31:24]) | - |
| 0x04 | VERSION | RO | - | version, ASCII "d.dd" (+0.01 at every source update) | - |
| 0x08 | DATE | RO | - | date of the last source update, BCD mm/dd/yyyy | - |
| 0x10 | CMD | RW | 0 | write starts a command (ignored and CMD_ERR while busy); reads back the last one | OPCODE[7:0] flash opcode; ADDR_EN[8] send the 3 address bytes; DUMMY[15:12] dummy bytes after the address; READ_DATA[16] LEN data bytes read to m_axis; WRITE_DATA[17] LEN data bytes written from s_axis |
| 0x14 | ADDR | RW | 0 | flash address (3 bytes) | - |
| 0x18 | LEN | RW | 0 | data bytes (0..65535) | - |
| 0x1C | CLKDIV | RW | 4 | sclk half period in clocks (minimum 3) | - |
| 0x20 | STATUS | CMD | 0 | status; write 1 to [2:1] to clear those flags | BUSY[0] command in progress; DONE[1] command finished (sticky, W1C); CMD_ERR[2] CMD written while busy (sticky, W1C) |
| 0x24 | IRQ_EN | RW | 0 | [0] irq_o = DONE | - |

The block is generated, not hand-written: write the JSON above and run `python3 ip/scripts/regmap_gen.py ip/peripherals/spi_flash_ctrl/src/include/spi_flash_ctrl_regs.json`, which also emits the C header and Markdown documentation. Extend the generator rather than editing its output.


## 7. Implementation constraints

- Synthesizable SystemVerilog-2012, technology independent (no vendor primitives; infer RAM and DSP).
- Must work in iverilog 12+ (`-g2012`), Verilator lint (`-Wall`, no UNOPTFLAT or latches) and Yosys.
- iverilog limits: declare before use; no enum ternaries without casts; no `break`; no arrays of queues; no `wait` on function calls; no declarations inside nested loop bodies of static initial blocks.
- No combinational path from a ready input back to a ready output; hoist scratch variables (no latches); split control and data `always_ff` blocks.
- One statement per line (`a <= b; c <= d;` is two lines; `if (x) y <= 1; else y <= 0;` is four).
- Instantiations: one parameter per line in `#( ... )` and one port per line, closing with `) u_name (` and `);` at the instance's indentation; a port-group macro is one port on its own line.
- Check with `python3 ip/scripts/sv_format.py --check <files>` (it can also rewrite: whitespace only, token-checked).
- Resources: Last Yosys synth_xilinx (7-series) result: about 457 LUTs, 504 flip-flops. Stay within about this budget.

## 9. Guidelines

Follow the design guidelines in `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md` (complete rules; this prompt wins where it sets a value explicitly). In short:

- Synthesizable, technology-independent SystemVerilog-2012; behavioural models behind `` `ifdef SYNTHESIS `` black boxes; iverilog / Verilator / Yosys clean.
- Layout: one statement per line; one parameter and one port per line in instantiations; two-space indent; a comment on every port.
- Naming: `lower_snake_case` modules and files, `u_` instances, `g_` generate blocks, `UPPER_CASE` parameters, `_i` / `_o` / `_n` / `_t` port suffixes, `s_axis_` / `m_axis_` / `s_axil_` buses.
- Clocks and resets per domain, every crossing through a CDC technique (see the clocks section).
- AXI4-Stream data with back-pressure, AXI4-Lite control (ID / INFO registers, SLVERR out of range), defined switch-over points for configuration changes.
- Self-checking testbench with an independent model, named `test_<what>` tasks in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, gaps and back-pressure, a mutation check, 100 % code coverage.
- Diagrams: module and instance names, arrows from output to input, no crossing lines, every clock and reset domain labelled.

Guidelines file: `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md`   (replace with your own guidelines file if needed)

## 12. Verification requirements

The reference testbench checks the following; the new testbench must cover at least the same:

```text
Self-checking testbench for spi_flash_ctrl with a
behavioral SPI NOR flash model (JEDEC ID, 03/0B read, 06/04 write
enable, 02 page program with 256 byte page wrap and AND-only
programming, 20 sector erase, 05 status with WIP/WEL). Tests read ID,
page program plus status polling, normal and fast read back, sector
erase, a read with stream back-pressure, a write with a slow source, a
command issued while busy (ignored, cmd_err), the done flag / irq and
W1C, and the CLKDIV setting. Prints TEST PASSED on success.
The test tasks are in tests/spi_flash_ctrl_tests.sv (`included).
```

Also: an independent reference model (not a copy of the RTL); random input gaps and output back-pressure on every stream; register readback; edge cases; a mutation check (break one rule, show the testbench fails).

Every simulation script names the tests it can run: `ip/scripts/run_sim.sh spi_flash_ctrl --list-tests` prints them (and every run prints them at its start). Put each test in its own `test_<what>` task in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, listed with a one-line description in that file's header.

Tests of the reference design (the new design must provide at least these):

| Testbench | Test | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `spi_flash_ctrl_tb` | `test_id_block` | ID "SPFL", VERSION ("d.dd"), DATE (BCD mm/dd/yyyy) at 0x00-0x08, read only (SLVERR); 0x0C reads 0 (register offsets from bfm.base = 0x10, the map after the ID block) |
| `spi_flash_ctrl_tb` | `test_idle` | cs_n high, sclk low after reset |
| `spi_flash_ctrl_tb` | `test_jedec_id` | 9Fh read ID: EF 40 17, tlast on the last byte; DONE W1C |
| `spi_flash_ctrl_tb` | `test_page_program` | Write enable, read status, page program |
| `spi_flash_ctrl_tb` | `test_read` | Read back with 03h and 0Bh (dummy byte) |
| `spi_flash_ctrl_tb` | `test_backpressure` | Read with m_axis back-pressure |
| `spi_flash_ctrl_tb` | `test_sector_erase` | Sector erase (20h) then the sector reads FF |
| `spi_flash_ctrl_tb` | `test_no_wel` | Program without write enable is ignored; slow source with page wrap |
| `spi_flash_ctrl_tb` | `test_busy_cmd` | A command while busy is ignored and sets CMD_ERR |

| `spi_flash_ctrl_tb` | `test_fast_clock` | CLKDIV below 3 runs at the minimum half period of 3 |

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Line (statement) | 100 % |
